subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Simplification of Tax Filing
description: A 60-second lesson on Simplification of Tax Filing.

hook.text: Estonia pre-fills tax returns with employer data. Citizens click confirm. Filing takes under 5 minutes.

buildup.text: Complex tax forms are a compliance barrier. Every additional step, form, and calculation creates friction that reduces.

discovery.text: Chetty found that the earned income tax credit goes unclaimed by millions who qualify.

twist.text: Tax preparation firms lobby against simplification. Their business depends on complexity.

climax.text: Pre-populated returns are the ultimate nudge: remove the effort entirely.

punchline.text: Make filing easy and people file. It isn't about willingness.

quiz.question: Why do millions of eligible people not claim the earned income tax credit?
options: They earn too much to qualify
The application process is too complex for those who need it most
They are unaware that taxes exist

details.summary: Simplifying tax filing by pre-filling returns with known information, reducing form complexity, and removing unnecessary decisions dramatically increases on-time filing rates and reduces errors, particularly benefiting lower-income taxpayers.
details.whyItMatters: Complex tax filing deters compliance and disproportionately burdens those with fewer resources. Simplification is a behavioral intervention that simultaneously reduces government collection costs and taxpayer frustration.
takeaways: Pre-filled returns increase filing rates and reduce errors significantly
Simplification benefits lower-income taxpayers the most
Many countries now offer pre-filled returns based on employer-reported data

faq.question: How does pre-filling tax returns improve compliance?
faq.answer: Pre-filled returns reduce the cognitive burden, time cost, and error risk of filing. When most information is already filled in, taxpayers only need to review and confirm. This removes the primary barriers that cause procrastination and non-filing.

faq.question: Why don't all countries pre-fill tax returns?
faq.answer: Political interests, tax preparation industry lobbying, and system complexity prevent adoption. In the US, the tax preparation industry actively lobbies against pre-filing because it would eliminate the need for their services.
